subsystems.name: Muscle actuator
subsystems.role: the living motor: contractile tissue that shortens when stimulated, replacing a motor or pneumatic muscle.
parts: skeletal muscle cells (primary myoblasts or stem-cell derived)
extracellular matrix proteins the cells secrete

subsystems.name: Scaffold and skeleton
subsystems.role: gives the tissue shape, keeps fibres aligned and transmits its pull to the robot.

subsystems.name: Life-support and perfusion
subsystems.role: keeps cells fed with oxygen, glucose and salts, and removes waste.

subsystems.name: Stimulation electrodes
subsystems.role: deliver the electrical pulses that trigger contraction and train the tissue.

subsystems.name: Sensing and control
subsystems.role: reads force and displacement and closes the control loop.

subsystems.name: Sterile housing
subsystems.role: keeps bacteria and fungi out, since the tissue has no immune system.

buildSteps.title: Get the cells
buildSteps.detail: A small muscle biopsy is taken and stem cells are reprogrammed, or an established muscle cell line is thawed; both give cells that can multiply indefinitely in a dish.

buildSteps.title: Expand the cells
buildSteps.detail: Cells are grown in flasks of warm nutrient medium at 37 °C until there are millions of them.

buildSteps.title: Cast the scaffold
buildSteps.detail: Cells are mixed into a soft gel and poured into a mould, often around flexible anchors that the cells will grip as they contract.

buildSteps.title: Form muscle fibres
buildSteps.detail: Over days the cells fuse into long, multinucleated fibres — the only stage that actually produces a contractile motor.

buildSteps.title: Anchor and align
buildSteps.detail: The fibres pull on their anchors and align along the tension lines, converting a shapeless gel into a directional actuator.

buildSteps.title: Train it
buildSteps.detail: Repeated electrical pulses, like exercise, thicken the fibres and build force output.

buildSteps.title: Wire up life support
buildSteps.detail: Perfusion channels, electrodes, sensors and a sterile housing are attached; without continuous nutrient flow the tissue dies within days.

buildSteps.title: Integrate and run
buildSteps.detail: The living module is bolted into the robot's skeleton and driven by the control electronics — for now, only on a bench or in a dish.

prerequisites.why: growing muscle cells outside a body is routine; keeping them alive and contracting for months is not.
the tissue must grip something soft enough not to tear itself apart when it pulls.
there is no blood supply, so every cell must sit within about 0.2 mm of a nutrient channel.
electrodes and wiring must flex with the tissue instead of cutting it.
living tissue in a machine has no immune system and no skin, so infection ends its life quickly.

pathway.milestone: single muscle-powered grippers, swimmers and walkers operating in dishes for days
pathway.unlocks: proof that lab-grown tissue can move a machine at all.

pathway.milestone: perfused constructs that survive and work for months rather than days
pathway.unlocks: repeated, reliable motion instead of one-off demonstrations.

pathway.milestone: stacked or bundled actuators reaching useful force and stroke
pathway.unlocks: real prosthetics and soft-robot limbs driven by muscle.

pathway.milestone: self-repairing bio-hybrid devices with on-board nutrient supply
pathway.unlocks: robots that heal minor damage and run without a tethered life-support line.
